name: 豚骨魚介ラーメン 穣 (Tonkotsu Gyokai Ramen Minoru)

claims.text: House-made wheat noodles are central to every bowl, so a shared boiling pot and wheat-laden kitchen make cross-contamination effectively unavoidable for a celiac.

No tare/seasoning ingredients are published, but a tonkotsu-gyokai ramen of this style almost always relies on a wheat-based shoyu tare; assume the seasoning contains wheat unless confirmed otherwise.
Broth is built on pork bone and fish/dried sardine and toppings are pork chashu, so there is no plant-based preparation and animal products are throughout the kitchen.
Noodles are made in-house and the shop emphasizes handmade quality and domestic ingredients, so staff know their components well even though no formal allergy program is described.

name: 鶏そば あやむや 烏丸店 (Torisoba Ayam-YA Karasuma)

claims.text: Core menu is wheat ramen and tsukemen noodles with shoyu/shio/miso tare; no gluten-free preparation is offered, so cross-contamination with wheat is inherent to the kitchen.
The signature basic bowl is a soy-sauce (shoyu) chicken soba; Japanese soy sauce tare is normally wheat-based, so the soy bowls should be assumed to contain wheat.
The house broth is tori-paitan (chicken) and the menu is chicken-centered, so a meat-free or vegan bowl is not advertised and would share equipment with chicken broth.

The shop is halal-certified through the Malaysia Halal Corporation and keeps the kitchen free of pork and alcohol, indicating a kitchen used to strict ingredient control, though this addresses religious requirements rather than allergens.
Cooks without chemical seasonings and builds umami from chicken and seafood aromatics, with no pork and no alcohol in the kitchen.

name: つけ麺 京都わたなべ (Tsukemen Kyoto Watanabe)

claims.text: Tsukemen dipping tare is conventionally based on wheat-containing soy sauce; no allergen breakdown is published for this shop.
All five broths share a pork-chicken bone and seafood base, including the vegetable-potato option, so no broth is free of animal products.

name: つけめんTETSU イオンモールKYOTO (Tsukemen TETSU AEON Mall KYOTO)

claims.text: Wheat noodles boiled in shared water in a single open food-court kitchen; no gluten-free handling. Not suitable for celiac diners.
Tsukemen broth/tare uses wheat-based shoyu and miso; the noodles themselves are wheat (blended with udon flour).
All bowls are based on pork-bone-and-seafood broth with pork chashu; no separate vegan prep area.

name: 和醸良麺 すがり (Wajo Ryomen Sugari)

claims.text: Core dish uses house-made wheat noodles (both noodle options — whole-wheat and yuzu — are wheat) cooked in shared water, making the kitchen unsuitable for gluten avoidance.

No allergen or tare ingredient disclosure is published; as a standard motsu tsukemen shop the seasoning base is expected to include wheat-based soy sauce, but this is not confirmed on any fetched page.
Both menu items are animal-based (chicken-paitan + seafood dashi broth with beef hoso offal); no plant-based option exists, so all dishes involve meat/fish.

name: 和麺ぐり虎 京都本店 (Wamen Guriko Kyoto Honten)

claims.text: Custom noodles are made from 100% domestic wheat flour and are handled throughout the kitchen; there is no gluten-free option or separate preparation, so wheat cross-contact is unavoidable.
The signature bowls are salt-based (shio) rather than soy-sauce-based; however, a separate fresh-soy-sauce (生醤油) ramen is also offered, which would contain wheat-based soy sauce.
All broths are animal-based (chicken consommé with clam, or wild sea bream) and the tare includes bonito dashi; no plant-based broth is prepared, so there is no vegan-safe bowl.
Bowls are shio (salt) tare rather than the usual wheat-shoyu tare, so the base seasoning is comparatively lower in soy/wheat than many ramen — though the wheat noodles still rule it out for celiacs.

name: 焼飯と麺 京都 (Yakimeshi to Men Kyoto)

claims.text: House-made wheat noodles and wheat-based shoyu tare are central to every bowl, and fried rice is cooked on the same line — heavy shared wheat presence throughout the kitchen.
The broth is a soy-sauce (shoyu) ramen and the char siu is marinated in soy sauce; standard Japanese shoyu contains wheat, so the tare and marinade should be assumed to contain wheat.
Broth is a pork-and-dried-fish (niboshi, bonito) stock and dishes feature pork char siu and egg; no plant-based preparation is mentioned.

name: 屋台ラーメン 京都中華そば 徳光 (Yatai Ramen Kyoto Chuka Soba Tokumitsu)

claims.text: Single-operator truck-bed yatai serving wheat-noodle ramen in one shared pot/workspace; no separate gluten-free prep is possible and none is advertised.
Broth is a pork-bone soy-sauce (shoyu) base — 「豚骨醤油のスープにたっぷりの背脂」 — and the shoyu tare typically contains wheat. Not gluten-free.
Every bowl is pork-bone broth with back fat and chashu; there is no vegan/vegetarian option and all prep shares the pork-based broth.
